login.title: Sign in to ASAPify
login.lede: Manage regional notifications. Operators also get map and decision access.
login.note: Demo: you sign in without an account, and all data inside is fictional.
login.rule_t: How a peat region is rated
login.rule: Every 10 minutes, Himawari-9 and GK2A are read for each peat region: a hotspot both satellites see at night can raise it to Alert, VIIRS and NASA POWER add support, and humidity and cloud are weighed. Alert calls an AI agent that checks NASA FIRMS hotspots, and an operator decides what goes out.
about.title: Early warning for peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan
about.lede: ASAPify reads Himawari-9 and GK2A every 10 minutes over 65 peat regions: two geostationary satellites that look at the same peat from different angles and confirm each other. A hotspot both see at night, at the same place, can raise a region to Alert; VIIRS and NASA POWER only add support. On Alert an AI agent checks NASA FIRMS fire hotspots, and an operator decides whether subscribers in that province are told.
about.scope: Coverage: peat in 11 provinces of Sumatra and Kalimantan, as 65 NASA POWER grid cells (0.5° × 0.625°) that each hold at least 25 km² of mapped peat. Every satellite pixel in a cell is scored and the ones on peat are marked. A slot reaches ASAPify 20–30 minutes after the satellites scan it.
about.name: The name comes from asap, Indonesian for smoke.
about.step1_d: Himawari-9 (140.7° E) and GK2A (128.2° E) brightness temperatures at 3.9 and 10.4 µm, 2 km pixels, from NOAA's open data. Cloud is read from the 10.4 µm channel itself.
about.step2_d: ΔBT = 3.9 µm − 10.4 µm, against the clear pixels of the same cell, slot and satellite. A pixel is fire-like only if the 3.9 µm channel itself also rose: thin cloud raises ΔBT without it.
about.step3_d: Both satellites hot within 8 km confirm each other. Trapezoid memberships turn ΔT and humidity into a utility for Safe, Warning and Alert; VIIRS and POWER near the hotspot can only raise Alert. By day, with one satellite or when the two disagree, the status stops at Warning. Cloud over 60 % means Not observable. Every change of status is recorded.
about.step4_d: On entering Alert, or when an operator asks, a Gemini agent built with Google ADK calls fetch_firms_data for VIIRS hotspots and answers Confirmed, Rejected or Needs manual review in YAML. The backend checks its numbers against what the tool returned.
about.step5_d: The operator publishes or rejects each verification. Only published alerts reach subscribers who chose that province, by Telegram DM and in the web inbox.
about.ai_rule: The status comes only from the data and the rules. The AI agent reads evidence for the operator and cannot change a status.
about.st_warning: Medium anomaly (about 3–6 K), or a stronger one seen by day or by only one of the two satellites. Closer monitoring; no agent call.
about.st_noobs: Cloud over more than 60 % of the cell in both views, or no satellite data. Never counted as safe.
about.st_safe: No fire-like anomaly that both satellites see.
about.limit1: A 2–4 km geostationary pixel sees larger fires; small or smouldering ones often stay below its detection limit, where VIIRS (375 m) still sees them.
about.limit2: Clouds hide the ground from both satellites; such regions are Not observable, never Safe.
about.limit3: In daylight the 3.9 µm channel also sees reflected sunlight, so day slots reach Warning at most.
about.limit4: A FIRMS hotspot is a thermal detection, not proof of fire. No imagery is checked, so the agent never claims that smoke was seen.
about.limit5: The peat map in use (KHG) is incomplete, so a fire anywhere in the cell counts, marked on or off mapped peat.
about.data_note: All processing runs on Google Cloud: Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Firestore, Vertex AI (Gemini) and the Agent Development Kit.
about.src_himawari: Bands 7 and 13 (3.9 and 10.4 µm), 2 km, every 10 minutes; JMA, via NOAA Open Data on AWS
about.src_gk2a: Channels SW038 and IR105 (3.8 and 10.5 µm), 2 km, every 10 minutes; KMA, via NOAA Open Data on AWS
about.src_power: Hourly skin temperature and humidity, 0.5° × 0.625°, about 2–3 days behind: support only
about.src_firms: NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 near-real-time hotspots, 375 m: support near a possible hotspot, and the agent's evidence
about.src_khg: Indicative map of peat hydrological units, KLHK
